BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Departures from Buyer Playbook; recommended pushback
**Status:** Seller documents treated as the other side's draft. No Amelia Frost fallback approvals are on file; all positions below are at our starting position.

---

## 1. Executive summary

The Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced." It is not. Read against our playbook, the Seller Update departs on **every** liability-regime item, and the Disclosure Letter — which is actually more candid than the cover note — confirms that the matters the Seller says are "addressed" (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses) are in fact **unresolved**. The two documents contradict each other, and that contradiction is our best leverage.

Three structural points dominate:

1. **A hidden general-regime override.** Clauses 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5 and the Fundamental/Title proposal, taken together, would pull title, capacity, fraud, Tax, IP and the specific indemnity into the 20% / 18-month / AUD 250k-basket regime. This is the single most important thing to reject.
2. **Blanket disclosure plus blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion.** Schedule 7 and clause 8.3 together would mean that anything in the data room or on a public register is both disclosed *and* "known," so no warranty claim could survive. That hollows out the warranty package entirely.
3. **Completion deliverables are not actually delivered.** The Disclosure Letter confirms no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark payout/discharge, no Ironquay receipt or assignment, and AUD 420,000 of bonuses missing from the funds flow.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 General Warranty cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a *conditional fallback only* with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None exists.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller has opened at exactly our fallback. That is not a coincidence we should reward; it may reflect a leak, a guess, or market norms, but either way we have no authority to accept it. Accepting it now also forfeits trading room on the other limitation terms.
- **Push back:** Revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is within range. If the team wants to use 20% as a trade, obtain Amelia Frost's written approval first, referencing this specific draft.

### 2.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's numbers are 5x ours on both thresholds, and the excess-only ("deductible") mechanic turns the basket into a permanent AUD 250,000 loss for the Buyer. For a AUD 24m business with a ~AUD 3.6m single-customer concentration, a AUD 25,000 de minimis would exclude a large proportion of realistic operational claims (e.g., individual Sandbar renewals at AUD 110,000 would clear it, but many employee, tax or contract items would not).
- **Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket. The deductible mechanic is a hard reject.

### 2.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims; plus "any limitation applying to Claims applies to **all Claims** unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Fundamental/Title at least six years.
- **Reasoning:** Two separate problems. (a) 18 months is our fallback, not our position — same point as the cap. (b) The second sentence is the override: it would apply the 18-month period (and by extension the cap and basket) to Fundamental, Tax, IP, indemnity and covenant claims unless we have *expressly* carved each one out. That reverses the drafting burden onto us and is inconsistent with the playbook requirement to keep categories separate with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Push back:** 24 months general. Delete the "applies to all Claims" sentence entirely; replace with a positive statement that the general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and that each other category has its own regime.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title claims
- **Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** separate regime; 100% cap; at least six years; outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing; a 20% cap would leave AUD 19.2m unrecoverable. This is the clearest departure in the draft and should be treated as non-negotiable.
- **Push back:** Reject in full. Separate Fundamental Warranty regime: 100% of price, 6 years minimum, no de minimis/basket, not subject to disclosure or buyer-knowledge qualifiers.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.
- **Reasoning:** "All Claims of any nature" on its face would purport to cap and time-bar fraud. Even where such a provision is unenforceable as to fraud, we should not have to litigate the point, and the clause would also sweep in the specific indemnity and covenant claims.
- **Push back:** Insert an express, overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out that sits above the whole of clause 12 and clauses 9.3 and 20.5. Confine exclusive remedy and non-reliance to general Warranty Claims only.

### 2.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records.
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Whole-data-room disclosure reverses the purpose of warranties — the Seller warrants, then says "but everything in the room is disclosed against it." Public-register disclosure is worse: it disclose matters neither side has looked at. Note also that the data-room cut-off (22 Sept) predates today; anything added since is unaccounted for.
- **Push back:** Delete 1.1 and the public-register limb of 1.2. Replace with: disclosure is effective only if made specifically in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Fix the Disclosure Letter at signing with no updating right except by consent.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Playbook:** delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Reasoning:** This is the mirror image of 2.6. "Discoverable" is constructive knowledge — it attributes to us everything we *could* have found, including by advisers, whether or not anyone did. Combined with Schedule 7, it leaves no surviving warranty claim. It also appears to be drafted as applying across the board, so it would bar title and indemnity claims.
- **Push back:** Delete clause 8.3. If a knowledge concept is to survive at all, it should be the Seller's knowledge (named individuals, after due enquiry) qualifying specific warranties — not a Buyer-knowledge exclusion of claims.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL para 2)
- **Seller Update:** "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Disclosure Letter:** consent has **NOT** been obtained; no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient.
- **Reasoning:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. The Seller Update says it's addressed; the Seller's own Disclosure Letter says it isn't. "Satisfied on delivery" would mean a conditional consent (e.g., subject to a price review, or a guarantee from the Buyer) counts as satisfied the moment the paper arrives, regardless of whether the 11.3 conditions can or will be met. "Reasonable endeavours" also gives the Seller an exit from the obligation.
- **Push back:** Condition precedent: unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 (or consent with all 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied) in form approved by the Buyer. Seller obligation: all reasonable endeavours at minimum, with the Buyer entitled to engage directly with Bluefen. Buyer-only waiver right. Consider a price-adjustment or termination right if consent is not obtained by the longstop.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL para 3)
- **Seller Update:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Disclosure Letter:** facility NOT repaid; no final discharge of security in the data room.
- **Playbook:** current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Reasoning:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. If the facility is not repaid at Completion from the price, the Buyer acquires a company carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt and is dependent on the Seller to procure a release later. A post-completion release is a credit risk on the Seller and leaves Riverlark's security in place over the business we have just bought. Also check DD-003 cl 8.1 — the share sale itself is likely a change-of-control trigger.
- **Push back:** Payout letter dated no earlier than two business days before Completion; repayment direct to Riverlark from Completion funds; executed deeds of release/discharge and PPSR releases as Completion deliverables. If the Seller insists on post-completion mechanics, that requires an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval — which we do not have, so our answer today is no.

### 2.10 Employee bonuses (Funds flow; DL para 5)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Disclosure Letter:** bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment; do not appear in the funds flow; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Reasoning:** "A matter for the Seller" is only meaningful if the Seller actually pays. Because the bonuses are triggered by Completion and conditioned on continued employment, the paying entity after Completion is Paperbark — i.e., us. If they are not in the funds flow and not treated as Debt / a Transaction Expense, the Buyer absorbs AUD 420,000 plus superannuation, payroll tax and any other on-costs. The Disclosure Letter's silence on on-costs is itself a gap.
- **Push back:** Either (a) include bonuses plus all on-costs as a specific line item deducted from the price in the funds flow, or (b) express Seller indemnity and pre-Completion payment by the Seller with evidence. Require the Seller to quantify on-costs in the Disclosure Letter.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL para 4)
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate."
- **Disclosure Letter:** DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not independent verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Reasoning:** The risk is not the AUD 180,000 payment — it is that until every fee is paid, the SOW3 IP has not transferred to Paperbark. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the cash but not the consequence: a third-party claim to IP, loss of licensing rights, or rework cost. We should not take a position on whether the AUD 180,000 is actually owed; we should make the Seller prove payment and transfer either way.
- **Push back:** Keep the cure path (Seller pays any outstanding SOW3 fees pre-Completion and delivers Ironquay's receipt and a confirmatory assignment). Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of title to or transfer of SOW3 Project Materials, outside the general cap/basket/time limits. Ask the Seller to produce bank evidence of payment status.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL para 6)
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
- **Disclosure Letter:** download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); access, scope and notification requirement all undetermined; investigation preliminary; no confirmed breach, no loss amount.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Reasoning:** We should neither accept "not material" nor assert that it is a breach. The honest position is that nobody knows yet. The Seller's characterisation is premature; so would be any demand from us for a specific sum.
- **Push back:** Pre-Completion covenant: preserve all access/download logs and link-tracking data; complete the investigation (including confirmation whether the link was accessed, and by whom); deliver written updates and the final report; notify regulators/individuals only if the investigation concludes it is required, with Buyer consultation. Specific disclosure limited to the facts actually stated in para 6. Reserve the position on a specific indemnity pending the report; do not price it now.

### 2.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (DL para 8)
- **Seller:** "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Disclosure Letter:** three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; read DD-008 and DD-011 together; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's label is a conclusion, not a disclosure. The fact the three must be "read together for timing/scope" suggests they may be a single AUD 330,000 commitment split in three, which matters for whether the amount is accrued pre-Completion (Seller's cost) or a genuine forward operating cost (Buyer's). We should not reflexively treat it as Debt.
- **Push back:** Require the Seller to state, for each renewal: commencement date, termination rights, whether any amount is accrued or invoiced before Completion, and whether the renewal is committed or optional. Decide classification (ordinary course vs. accrued liability / Debt) only once answered. Preserve the point in the working-capital/Debt definitions.

### 2.14 Tax / IP (Seller Update)
- **Seller:** "settled under the general regime above."
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Reasoning:** Nothing has been agreed. Folding Tax and IP into the 20%/18-month regime is the override in 2.3 applied by assertion. Equally, we should not overreach by claiming unlimited liability — the playbook does not authorise that.
- **Push back:** Record in the mark-up that Tax and IP are open and subject to separate regimes to be negotiated (tax warranty/indemnity typically with its own longer period; IP with its own cap tier). Do not accept the "settled" characterisation.

### 2.15 Title (Seller Update; DL para 10)
- **Seller:** title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Disclosure Letter:** DD-012 is the source relied on; does not state the Buyer has verified.
- **Playbook:** require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Reasoning:** The register is maintained by the Company, controlled by the Seller. It is evidence of what the Company records, not independent proof that no third party has an interest, that the shares are unencumbered (Riverlark's security may extend to the shares — check), or that Harbourglass has authority to sell.
- **Push back:** Completion deliverables: ASIC company extract; PPSR search against the Company and against the shares; Riverlark confirmation that no security over the shares subsists post-discharge; Seller board/shareholder resolutions and constitutional authority; share certificates (or lost-certificate indemnity); legal opinion or officer's certificate on title and capacity. Title warranties on the Fundamental regime (2.4).

### 2.16 Minor matters (DL paras 7, 9)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only, not landlord consent. Acceptable on its face, but confirm the notification is given pre-Completion and that there is no change-of-control termination right buried elsewhere in the lease.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** assignment restriction, no stated change-of-control trigger. Acceptable on its face; confirm by reading the full contract rather than relying on the Seller's summary.

---

## 3. Cross-cutting observations

- **Internal inconsistency as leverage.** The Seller Update says Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and the bonuses are "addressed"/"adequate"/"a matter for the Seller." The Seller's own Disclosure Letter says none of them is resolved. Our reply should quote the Disclosure Letter back at the Seller on each.
- **Disclosure Letter para 1.4 (no admissions)** means nothing in the letter can be used against the Seller as an acknowledgement. Combined with 1.1–1.2 and cl 8.3, the Seller's package would give it the benefit of disclosure without the burden of admission. Delete 1.4 or confine it so it does not undermine specific disclosures.
- **Our fallbacks are exposed.** The Seller has opened at our cap and time-limit fallbacks exactly. Whether coincidence or otherwise, the team should assume the Seller may know our range and hold the line accordingly. Check information-handling on our side.
- **Data room cut-off.** 22 September 2026 is six weeks ago. Request a bring-down and confirm no additions since; refuse any disclosure of post-cut-off material by reference.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m**; 20% only with Amelia Frost written approval (none held) |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k / excess-only | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k / first-dollar** |
| 3 | General claims period | 18 months | **24 months**; 18 only with Amelia Frost approval (none held) |
| 4 | "Limitations apply to all Claims" | Included | **Delete**; general regime applies to general Warranty Claims only |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **Separate regime**: 100%, 6+ years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar |
| 6 | Fraud/wilful concealment | Caught by "all Claims" | **Express overriding carve-out** from all caps, baskets, limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | **Specific fair disclosure only**; delete 1.1, public-register limb of 1.2 |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | **Delete** |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **CP**: effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met pre-Completion |
| 10 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | **Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion**; post-Completion only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval |
| 11 | Bonuses (AUD 420k) | Not itemised | **Line item incl. on-costs** or seller-funded with evidence |
| 12 | Ironquay | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | **Broaden** to loss from failure of IP transfer; keep cure; demand proof of payment/assignment |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Preserve logs, investigate, updates**; no characterisation either way; reserve indemnity |
| 14 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | **Assess** with further information; no automatic Debt treatment |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | **Open**; separate regimes to be negotiated |
| 16 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence** (ASIC, PPSR, resolutions, certificates, Riverlark confirmation) |
| 17 | DL 1.4 no-admissions | Included | Delete or confine |

**Approvals required before any concession:** none of items 1, 3 or 10 may move from our starting position without Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given; the mark-up should be prepared on our starting positions throughout.

**Suggested next steps:**
1. Prepare a full mark-up of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter on the above basis.
2. Issue a supplementary RFI to the Seller covering: Bluefen consent status and 11.3 conditions; Riverlark payout and security scope (including over the shares); Ironquay payment evidence and confirmatory assignment; bonus on-cost quantification; DD-006 log preservation and investigation report; Sandbar renewal terms; full DD-007 and DD-009 contracts.
3. Confirm internally how the Seller arrived at our two fallback figures.

2. **Blanket disclosure plus blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion.** Schedule 7 and clause 8.3 together would mean that anything in the data room or on a public register is both disclosed *and* "known," so no warranty claim could survive. That hollows out the warranty package entirely.
3. **Completion deliverables are not actually delivered.** The Disclosure Letter confirms no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark payout/discharge, no Ironquay receipt or assignment, and AUD 420,000 of bonuses missing from the funds flow.

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 General Warranty cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a *conditional fallback only* with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None exists.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller has opened at exactly our fallback. That is not a coincidence we should reward; it may reflect a leak, a guess, or market norms, but either way we have no authority to accept it. Accepting it now also forfeits trading room on the other limitation terms.
- **Push back:** Revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is within range. If the team wants to use 20% as a trade, obtain Amelia Frost's written approval first, referencing this specific draft.

### 2.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's numbers are 5x ours on both thresholds, and the excess-only ("deductible") mechanic turns the basket into a permanent AUD 250,000 loss for the Buyer. For a AUD 24m business with a ~AUD 3.6m single-customer concentration, a AUD 25,000 de minimis would exclude a large proportion of realistic operational claims (e.g., individual Sandbar renewals at AUD 110,000 would clear it, but many employee, tax or contract items would not).
- **Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket. The deductible mechanic is a hard reject.

### 2.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims; plus "any limitation applying to Claims applies to **all Claims** unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Fundamental/Title at least six years.
- **Reasoning:** Two separate problems. (a) 18 months is our fallback, not our position — same point as the cap. (b) The second sentence is the override: it would apply the 18-month period (and by extension the cap and basket) to Fundamental, Tax, IP, indemnity and covenant claims unless we have *expressly* carved each one out. That reverses the drafting burden onto us and is inconsistent with the playbook requirement to keep categories separate with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Push back:** 24 months general. Delete the "applies to all Claims" sentence entirely; replace with a positive statement that the general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and that each other category has its own regime.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title claims
- **Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** separate regime; 100% cap; at least six years; outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing; a 20% cap would leave AUD 19.2m unrecoverable. This is the clearest departure in the draft and should be treated as non-negotiable.
- **Push back:** Reject in full. Separate Fundamental Warranty regime: 100% of price, 6 years minimum, no de minimis/basket, not subject to disclosure or buyer-knowledge qualifiers.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.
- **Reasoning:** "All Claims of any nature" on its face would purport to cap and time-bar fraud. Even where such a provision is unenforceable as to fraud, we should not have to litigate the point, and the clause would also sweep in the specific indemnity and covenant claims.
- **Push back:** Insert an express, overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out that sits above the whole of clause 12 and clauses 9.3 and 20.5. Confine exclusive remedy and non-reliance to general Warranty Claims only.

### 2.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records.
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Whole-data-room disclosure reverses the purpose of warranties — the Seller warrants, then says "but everything in the room is disclosed against it." Public-register disclosure is worse: it disclose matters neither side has looked at. Note also that the data-room cut-off (22 Sept) predates today; anything added since is unaccounted for.
- **Push back:** Delete 1.1 and the public-register limb of 1.2. Replace with: disclosure is effective only if made specifically in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Fix the Disclosure Letter at signing with no updating right except by consent.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Playbook:** delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Reasoning:** This is the mirror image of 2.6. "Discoverable" is constructive knowledge — it attributes to us everything we *could* have found, including by advisers, whether or not anyone did. Combined with Schedule 7, it leaves no surviving warranty claim. It also appears to be drafted as applying across the board, so it would bar title and indemnity claims.
- **Push back:** Delete clause 8.3. If a knowledge concept is to survive at all, it should be the Seller's knowledge (named individuals, after due enquiry) qualifying specific warranties — not a Buyer-knowledge exclusion of claims.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL para 2)
- **Seller Update:** "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Disclosure Letter:** consent has **NOT** been obtained; no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient.
- **Reasoning:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. The Seller Update says it's addressed; the Seller's own Disclosure Letter says it isn't. "Satisfied on delivery" would mean a conditional consent (e.g., subject to a price review, or a guarantee from the Buyer) counts as satisfied the moment the paper arrives, regardless of whether the 11.3 conditions can or will be met. "Reasonable endeavours" also gives the Seller an exit from the obligation.
- **Push back:** Condition precedent: unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 (or consent with all 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied) in form approved by the Buyer. Seller obligation: all reasonable endeavours at minimum, with the Buyer entitled to engage directly with Bluefen. Buyer-only waiver right. Consider a price-adjustment or termination right if consent is not obtained by the longstop.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL para 3)
- **Seller Update:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Disclosure Letter:** facility NOT repaid; no final discharge of security in the data room.
- **Playbook:** current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Reasoning:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. If the facility is not repaid at Completion from the price, the Buyer acquires a company carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt and is dependent on the Seller to procure a release later. A post-completion release is a credit risk on the Seller and leaves Riverlark's security in place over the business we have just bought. Also check DD-003 cl 8.1 — the share sale itself is likely a change-of-control trigger.
- **Push back:** Payout letter dated no earlier than two business days before Completion; repayment direct to Riverlark from Completion funds; executed deeds of release/discharge and PPSR releases as Completion deliverables. If the Seller insists on post-completion mechanics, that requires an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval — which we do not have, so our answer today is no.

### 2.10 Employee bonuses (Funds flow; DL para 5)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Disclosure Letter:** bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment; do not appear in the funds flow; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Reasoning:** "A matter for the Seller" is only meaningful if the Seller actually pays. Because the bonuses are triggered by Completion and conditioned on continued employment, the paying entity after Completion is Paperbark — i.e., us. If they are not in the funds flow and not treated as Debt / a Transaction Expense, the Buyer absorbs AUD 420,000 plus superannuation, payroll tax and any other on-costs. The Disclosure Letter's silence on on-costs is itself a gap.
- **Push back:** Either (a) include bonuses plus all on-costs as a specific line item deducted from the price in the funds flow, or (b) express Seller indemnity and pre-Completion payment by the Seller with evidence. Require the Seller to quantify on-costs in the Disclosure Letter.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL para 4)
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate."
- **Disclosure Letter:** DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not independent verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Reasoning:** The risk is not the AUD 180,000 payment — it is that until every fee is paid, the SOW3 IP has not transferred to Paperbark. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the cash but not the consequence: a third-party claim to IP, loss of licensing rights, or rework cost. We should not take a position on whether the AUD 180,000 is actually owed; we should make the Seller prove payment and transfer either way.
- **Push back:** Keep the cure path (Seller pays any outstanding SOW3 fees pre-Completion and delivers Ironquay's receipt and a confirmatory assignment). Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of title to or transfer of SOW3 Project Materials, outside the general cap/basket/time limits. Ask the Seller to produce bank evidence of payment status.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL para 6)
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
- **Disclosure Letter:** download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); access, scope and notification requirement all undetermined; investigation preliminary; no confirmed breach, no loss amount.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Reasoning:** We should neither accept "not material" nor assert that it is a breach. The honest position is that nobody knows yet. The Seller's characterisation is premature; so would be any demand from us for a specific sum.
- **Push back:** Pre-Completion covenant: preserve all access/download logs and link-tracking data; complete the investigation (including confirmation whether the link was accessed, and by whom); deliver written updates and the final report; notify regulators/individuals only if the investigation concludes it is required, with Buyer consultation. Specific disclosure limited to the facts actually stated in para 6. Reserve the position on a specific indemnity pending the report; do not price it now.

### 2.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (DL para 8)
- **Seller:** "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Disclosure Letter:** three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; read DD-008 and DD-011 together; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's label is a conclusion, not a disclosure. The fact the three must be "read together for timing/scope" suggests they may be a single AUD 330,000 commitment split in three, which matters for whether the amount is accrued pre-Completion (Seller's cost) or a genuine forward operating cost (Buyer's). We should not reflexively treat it as Debt.
- **Push back:** Require the Seller to state, for each renewal: commencement date, termination rights, whether any amount is accrued or invoiced before Completion, and whether the renewal is committed or optional. Decide classification (ordinary course vs. accrued liability / Debt) only once answered. Preserve the point in the working-capital/Debt definitions.

### 2.14 Tax / IP (Seller Update)
- **Seller:** "settled under the general regime above."
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Reasoning:** Nothing has been agreed. Folding Tax and IP into the 20%/18-month regime is the override in 2.3 applied by assertion. Equally, we should not overreach by claiming unlimited liability — the playbook does not authorise that.
- **Push back:** Record in the mark-up that Tax and IP are open and subject to separate regimes to be negotiated (tax warranty/indemnity typically with its own longer period; IP with its own cap tier). Do not accept the "settled" characterisation.

### 2.15 Title (Seller Update; DL para 10)
- **Seller:** title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Disclosure Letter:** DD-012 is the source relied on; does not state the Buyer has verified.
- **Playbook:** require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Reasoning:** The register is maintained by the Company, controlled by the Seller. It is evidence of what the Company records, not independent proof that no third party has an interest, that the shares are unencumbered (Riverlark's security may extend to the shares — check), or that Harbourglass has authority to sell.
- **Push back:** Completion deliverables: ASIC company extract; PPSR search against the Company and against the shares; Riverlark confirmation that no security over the shares subsists post-discharge; Seller board/shareholder resolutions and constitutional authority; share certificates (or lost-certificate indemnity); legal opinion or officer's certificate on title and capacity. Title warranties on the Fundamental regime (2.4).

### 2.16 Minor matters (DL paras 7, 9)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only, not landlord consent. Acceptable on its face, but confirm the notification is given pre-Completion and that there is no change-of-control termination right buried elsewhere in the lease.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** assignment restriction, no stated change-of-control trigger. Acceptable on its face; confirm by reading the full contract rather than relying on the Seller's summary.

## 3. Cross-cutting observations

- **Internal inconsistency as leverage.** The Seller Update says Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and the bonuses are "addressed"/"adequate"/"a matter for the Seller." The Seller's own Disclosure Letter says none of them is resolved. Our reply should quote the Disclosure Letter back at the Seller on each.
- **Disclosure Letter para 1.4 (no admissions)** means nothing in the letter can be used against the Seller as an acknowledgement. Combined with 1.1–1.2 and cl 8.3, the Seller's package would give it the benefit of disclosure without the burden of admission. Delete 1.4 or confine it so it does not undermine specific disclosures.
- **Our fallbacks are exposed.** The Seller has opened at our cap and time-limit fallbacks exactly. Whether coincidence or otherwise, the team should assume the Seller may know our range and hold the line accordingly. Check information-handling on our side.
- **Data room cut-off.** 22 September 2026 is six weeks ago. Request a bring-down and confirm no additions since; refuse any disclosure of post-cut-off material by reference.
